original_test_intent: Validate Tx equalization redo interoperability across the approved HGX PCIe path by proving every NVQual Test #25 redo completes the required equalization phases on all mapped lanes, returns the expected generation/width and NVIDIA device function, and causes no hang, unplanned reboot, or error.
original_method: Pin Test #25, path/lane topology, generation/width, equalization phase and preset/coefficient ownership, redo primitive, iterations/timing, transient and device/function acceptance; preserve baselines; record each redo's phase/lane/LTSSM/link/identity/error results durably before the next; stop on first marginal lane, failed redo, downtraining, or platform fault and recover out of band.
manual_activity: HGX owner/FAE approves the signal-training recipe, lane/path scope, parameters and long-run risk; an operator isolates the SUT, observes out-of-band health, and owns recovery from a degraded or lost link.
required_inputs: Pinned NVIDIA NVQual Test #25 Tx-eq package/configuration and compatible firmware/driver
Target generation/width, equalization phases, preset/coefficient ownership, redo primitive, settle deadline, transient and per-lane pass rules
Iteration count/timing, complete device/function acceptance, error policy, persistent storage, aborts, final state, and recovery
safety_requirements: Dedicated non-production HGX SUT with explicit signal-training and any reset/power authorization
No unsaved workload; verified BMC/console/power recovery; stable cooling/power
Do not alter presets or coefficients outside the pinned vendor recipe
Stop on failed phase, marginal lane, timeout, downtraining, missing/misbound device, driver/GPU failure, hang/reboot, new AER, thermal/power fault, tool failure, or evidence gap
No evidence clearing, reset escalation, load continuation, or automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate Test #25 configuration, path/lane identity, baseline, interlocks, ledger, and recovery
Run only the approved Tx-eq redo operation
Correlate signal state with NVIDIA, driver, OS, BMC, console, thermal, and power health
Do not invent coefficients, broaden scope, retry, force reset/power recovery, or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve Test #25 recipe, path/lane scope, equalization parameters, iterations, and service impact
Own first-fault disposition and out-of-band recovery
Review every redo transaction and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It identifies the Tx-eq purpose but provides no exact recipe or lane/equalization contract; final lspci/nvidia-smi evidence cannot prove every redo's training phases and transient behavior.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the pinned Test #25 recipe with an atomic redo ledger and block redo N+1 until N's phase/lane/LTSSM, negotiated link, complete device/function state, timing, and error results are durable.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: NVQual Test #25, Tx Eq Redo interoperability, all-items/no-hang/no-reboot Criteria, no bundle, and 5/600-minute allocation remain; missing iterations/parameters are not invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: CRITICAL INTERLOCKED HGX TX EQUALIZATION INTEROPERABILITY
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat each redo as a lane-aware signal-training transaction, binding pinned parameters and phases to settled link, identity-complete device/function recovery, errors, and platform health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds per-lane/phase semantics, complete device/function state, durable transactional evidence, first-fault inhibition, and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A final full-width link cannot reveal skipped redos, marginal lanes, failed intermediate phases, temporary downtraining, device-function loss, or recovered AER events.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Uncontrolled equalization parameters or repeated redos can destabilize a marginal link, remove GPUs, produce host resets, or obscure the first failing signal condition.

project_override_considerations: Vendor aggregate pass is acceptable only if the pinned artifact retains per-redo and per-lane/phase failure visibility. A generic retrain, SBR, link toggle, reboot, or power cycle does not substitute for Tx-eq redo coverage.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, owner-approved Test #25 manifest/configuration, and authorization
HGX/tool/firmware/driver/BMC identities plus path and per-lane topology
Per-redo phase/lane/equalization/LTSSM, timing, negotiated link, full NVIDIA identity/function, and disposition ledger
First-fault recovery or clean final link/device/host state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Test #25 Procedure, Criteria, and same-row AI review consistently identify Tx-equalization redo interoperability. Missing lane/parameter and acceptance details are readiness under-specification, not a competing source objective.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The Tx-eq interoperability objective is clear. Proprietary tooling, path/lane recipe, acceptance, isolation, evidence, and recovery are identifiable prerequisites rather than permanent review blockers.

review_improvement: Preserves Test #25 interoperability while requiring lane-aware equalization transactions and rejecting a recovered final link as proof of every redo.
independent_technical_reasoning: Tx equalization interoperability depends on both sides of a multi-component path honoring phase and coefficient exchanges at the target generation. A final negotiated link does not show whether an intermediate redo failed, a lane was marginal, or the endpoint briefly disappeared and recovered. Stable device identities, driver function and error chronology must therefore be committed with each lane-aware redo before another stimulus can overwrite the failure context.
